title: Personal Credit Cards: Penalty APR and Military Rate Cap
content:
Two rules on Personal Credit Cards move an account's APRs away from those set at approval: the penalty APR, which follows serious lateness, and the rate cap for customers on active military duty.

## Penalty APR

- The penalty APR takes the place of the purchase APR and the cash advance APR once a minimum payment is still unpaid the tier's trigger number of days after its due date, measured by the account's days past due.
- The account is repriced to the penalty APR only after a written notice period of 45 calendar days.
- On a tier that has no penalty APR, none is ever applied.
- The penalty APR is lifted, and the APRs held before it are restored, once the run of consecutive on-time minimum payments made after the penalty began reaches the tier's cure figure. A payment is on time for this purpose when the payments and credits posted between a statement's closing and its due date meet that statement's minimum.

## Military rate cap

The cap applies only while the customer's profile shows a military status of active duty, as recorded by the bank; the customer's own statement of service does not substitute for the profile. While it applies:

- every APR on the account is held at or below the cap, and the account is repriced with the cap in force;
- any penalty APR is suspended;
- the annual fee is not charged;
- for every cycle after the profile's status became active duty, whatever interest was charged beyond the cap is reversed, as to the excess only, on the military benefit ground.

When active duty ends, the cap comes off, and the APRs that applied before the cap reappear from the first statement following the change of status. The cap never lifts an APR that already lies below it.

| Tier | Military rate cap |
|---|---|
| Secured Visa | 6.00 percent |
| College Rewards Visa | 6.00 percent |
| Platinum Low Rate Visa | 6.00 percent |
| Cash Rewards Visa | 6.00 percent |
| Travel Rewards Visa Signature | 6.00 percent |
| Visa Infinite Private Client | 6.00 percent |

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A cycle's purchase interest of 42.00 USD was billed at 21.00 percent after the profile turned to active duty. At the 6.00 percent cap the same balance would have borne 12.00 USD, so 30.00 USD, the excess, is reversed. A balance already priced at 4.90 percent stays at 4.90 percent.
